page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz. The server is equipped with 168.0 GB of RAM, translating to an exceptionally high memory allocation of 42.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded text processing reaching top-tier status. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also demonstrate strong throughput. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores. Memory bandwidth is average for cached small-block operations but drops to weak for large-block uncached read and write operations.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require massive memory footprints but do not demand heavy parallelized multi-core processing. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, single-threaded data processing, caching layers, and database operations that fit entirely within its 168.0 GB RAM. It is less optimal for highly parallelized compute tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
